# Motion matrix

The grid below is generated from `motion.jsonl` -- the source of record, which
carries the provenance the `*` convention only hints at. Edit the jsonl and
regenerate; do not hand-edit this file.

HOW each component can move, and what each movement consumes. One row per
`(component, part, transition)`. A row declares mechanics and its complete consumption
set -- duration tier, curve role, delays, extents -- every dimension a first-class
column, none ever implied. A row never carries a raw value. Values live in the system
tokens (`--rafters-duration-fast` and kin); Studio says what `duration-fast` is; an
intent preset is nothing but a value-set for the system tokens. ZERO IS A VALUE.

Rows are assigned by need, not by cross-product. A cell exists because the component's
behaviour has that moment; no cell exists for a moment the component does not have.
Components that need a speed choice declare a variant in their own source (CVA, like
`size`) -- variants are in the component, not in this matrix, which records only the
default assignment.

Annotation provenance: unmarked assignments carry the July efficient baseline
(legion 019f956f). Assignments marked `*` are PROPOSED here and unreviewed -- treat
them as a starting position for the knobs, not as measured. Nothing in this file was
derived; there is no formula upstream of these cells.

This file supersedes the token-vocabulary matrix (branch `docs/motion-matrix`,
cca2d50e). The 13 semantic motion tokens are deleted by ruling (2026-08-02). The old
file's "holes" (thumb-travel, indicator-move, slide-advance, value-change, state-swap)
are movements here, not holes.

## Token generics -- five namespaces of equal rank

Every namespace gets its own `--rafters-*` vars and its own utilities (all generated by
us -- `--duration-*` is not a Tailwind v4 theme namespace, nothing rides on theme
inference). Studio writes the values.

| namespace | members | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `duration-*` | instant, micro, fast, moderate, normal, slow | banded ranges; band is perception, position is character |
| `ease-*` | standard, enter, exit, linear, spring-smooth, spring-snappy | roles; curve assignment is explicit per cell, never inferred from a transition's name |
| `delay-*` | hover-intent, linger, choreo-step, stagger-step, skip | first-class; replaces hardcoded 200ms in tooltip and navigation-menu. `skip` is the warm-reopen grace: moving between adjacent tooltips/hover targets while one was just open reopens without the intent delay |
| `extent-*` | pop (zoom start scale), press (depression scale), draw (indicator draw) | the geometry of a movement; half the personality lives here -- friendly pops big, elegant whispers in |
| `period-*` | spin, pulse, blink, shimmer | loops; intent-invariant by ruling but ride the same var mechanism so they remain reachable |

Slide distances stay geometric (percent of own size, or spacing-derived), marked
`structural` below -- as are fixed angles (a chevron's 180deg is mechanics, not tuning).

## Movement vocabulary -- mechanics, not tokens

| movement | properties | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fade` | opacity | |
| `slide` | transform: translate | axis, and a side where anchored |
| `zoom` | transform: scale | anchored popups scale from the anchor origin; consumes `extent-pop` |
| `rotate` | transform: rotate | never combined with translate (combination constraint) |
| `reveal` | grid-rows / height | disclosure on y |
| `travel` | position along a track | distance IS the travel; see the pointer rule |
| `fill` | inline-size / width | value displays |
| `swap` | discrete state change | at zero it is an instant swap, a legitimate personality |
| `color` | background, text, border | |
| `elevation` | box-shadow | |
| `ring` | outline / ring | focus |
| `loop` | keyframes, infinite | takes a period, not a duration |
| `delay` | time before/between movements | choreography |

**The pointer rule (travel):** while a pointer drives the part, the part tracks the
pointer EXACTLY -- no animation, not a tunable cell, any nonzero value is a defect.
The same part moving by a discrete step (keyboard, index change, snap on release)
animates, and the step distance is the travel.

**The anchor rule (reposition):** an open anchored popup tracking its anchor -- scroll,
resize, collision flip or shift (`collision-detector`, `float`) -- repositions
INSTANTLY. Never animated, not a tunable cell: an animated reposition reads as the
popup wandering. Only presence (open/close) animates; position while open is tracking,
same family as the pointer rule.

**Presence:** enter/exit cells assume keyframes on mount and behaviour-owned unmount --
the behaviour layer holds removal until the node's own animations have settled
(`use-presence` is the mechanism: it asks the node what is running and waits on that,
rather than timing the cell itself). No `@starting-style` dependency; it is not trusted
outside Tailwind's pipeline.

**Choreography:** parts sequence via `delay-choreo-step` between their rows. Collection
popups (marked C) carry an items row with `delay-stagger-step`; zero (all items
together) is the expected value for most intents.

**The input rule:** layout change driven by the user's own input stream -- textarea
autosize while typing, combobox list reflow per keystroke -- tracks instantly. Animating
it puts lag between a person and their own hands. Third member of the tracking family
(pointer rule, anchor rule).

**Reduced motion is law, not a cell:** every cell in this matrix resolves to zero under
`prefers-reduced-motion` except loops that communicate ongoing work (spinner, progress
indeterminate), which may slow but not stop -- stillness there reads as frozen. This is
system behaviour above every intent; no preset can override it.

**Logical directions:** slide sides and travel axes are logical (inline-start/end), not
physical -- RTL flips them for free. A cell that names a physical side is a defect.

**Out of scope for this matrix:** page-level transitions (framework/view-transition
territory -- the old `motion-page` token died with no consumer for exactly this reason);
scroll-driven reveals (site-level composition, not component behaviour); and
cross-component choreography (ruled out 2026-08-02: it requires global animation state
and this stack has none -- neither does the platform underneath it).

**Loops are intent-invariant** by standing ruling. Their cells exist here (the period
is a setting) but sit outside the intent presets.

### no rows

aspect-ratio, container, grid, kbd, label, separator, typography, button-group, empty,
field (wrapper itself), calendar (day cells -- selection is instant), badge.

Badge's variant colour is a prop change, not a behavioural moment -- no state machine,
no cell. Empty appears only by its parent's choice; the parent owns that motion. These
are exclusions by absence of behaviour, not values set to zero: a zero cell is tunable,
a missing row is a claim the moment does not exist. Contest the claim by finding the
behaviour, not by adding the row.

Two deliberate non-cells, recorded so they read as decisions*: enabled <-> disabled
snaps everywhere (state gating, not communication); alert-dialog has no close-button
row because a consequence-gated dialog deliberately has no casual dismiss affordance.

## Consumption

Components bake the generic in source: a classes file says `duration-fast
ease-standard`, resolving to `var(--rafters-duration-fast)` etc. Studio writes the
values; an intent preset is a value-set over the five namespaces. Two override planes:

- **value** -- retune what `duration-fast` is (the token override system, long solid);
- **assignment** -- move a cell off its tier: a component-declared variant where one
  exists, or your own component source (you own it).

JS-consumed cells (delays, travel, settle, presence timing) read the same
`--rafters-*` vars through a typed runtime accessor -- one token source, two
consumption surfaces. No cell is ever a named token; there is one `fast`, everywhere,
always.
